articles.title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing
articles.summary: All parties urge Welsh and UK ministers to ensure polluters pay to clean up contaminated land.
articles.body:
Member of the Senedd from all parties have urged Welsh ministers to work with the UK government to make sure polluters pay for cleaning up contaminated land.

A motion introduced by Plaid Cymru MS Niamh Salkeld, backed across party lines, also calls for a UK fund to investigate and remediate sites where costs cannot be recovered, and for a framework to test affected land.

The calls come after a BBC documentary by Michael Sheen examined claims toxic waste poisoned people at 14 sites in Wales and England.

A Welsh government minister promised a plan to "progressively restore post-industrial land" and protect communities from "potential risks".

Earlier this month, Sheen went to Westminster to urge MPs to support a testing programme.

In the Senedd on Thursday, one member after another recounted in detail the history of sites in their area that they were worried about.

Salkeld, who represents the constituency of Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, said her motion was about "making sure that the legacy of our industrial past is managed properly and fairly".

"It's about having a clearer national picture of contaminated land," she said.

"It's about prioritising the sites where the risks are greatest.

"It's about giving local authorities the support that they need, and it's about making sure that where possible, those responsible for pollution contribute to the cost of putting it right.

"The communities living alongside these sites did not create this contamination, so they should not be left with carrying the uncertainty, the potential risks, all the costs."

What he told me made my blood run cold - Michael Sheen investigates Wales' toxic legacy

Toxic waste sites exposed in Michael Sheen documentary are 'tip of the iceberg'

A number of speakers highlighted the results of a Freedom of Information inquiry by the environmental campaign group Friends of the Earth , indicating there were potentially over 45,000 contaminated land sites in Wales, with only 82 sites being designated as contaminated.

Reform MS Andrew Griffin said communities across Wales living near sites that are potentially unsafe "deserve answers".

"They deserve a system capable of establishing the facts, and where action is needed, they deserve to know that the money and the determination are there to see it through.

"As their representatives, the least we can do is to make sure their questions are heard and keep asking them until they get a proper answer."

Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates highlighted a combined pledge of more than £240m from the previous Welsh government, led by his party, and Labour ministers at Westminster for coal tip remediation.

He said this demonstrated "that all levels of government need to act fast and need to act together in partnership" to tackle this pollution.

"Councils, citizens and communities cannot afford the cost of remediation, nor can they afford to wait any longer for action."

He called on Plaid Cymru ministers to "stand up for the people of Wales by taking urgent action where it can now".

Conservative Janet Finch-Saunders said local communities "should be able to understand where these sites are located, what risks have been identified, what action is being taken, and whether that action is satisfactory".

"Regular inspections and up-to-date public registers would help," she said.

"We must ensure that lessons are learned from previous incidents where contamination occurs, the response should be timely, coordinated, and proportionate, with clear responsibility for investigating the source.

"This is not simply about dealing with contamination after it has occurred. It is about prevention, enforcement, and accountability."

Rural Resilience and Sustainability Minister Llyr Gruffydd promised the Welsh government was "absolutely committed to developing a Wales-wide strategy to progressively restore post-industrial land and to protect communities from those potential risks that come with that legacy".

He said he had heard the "calls for action", pledging he would "ensure that former industrial land is made safe".

"I will protect public health and deliver long-overdue environmental justice for the communities that have been most affected by this," he added.

The motion was passed with no objections.

articles.title: Musk volta ao governo Trump em projeto sobre o futuro da guerra | G1
articles.standfirst: Movimento consolida reaproximação de Musk e Trump pouco mais de um ano após sua saída conturbada do Departamento de Eficiência Governamental (DOGE). Bilionário dono da Space X, da Tesla e do X liderará estudo militar sobre guerra, segundo o Pentágono.
articles.summary: Movimento consolida reaproximação de Musk e Trump pouco mais de um ano após sua saída conturbada do Departamento de Eficiência Governamental (DOGE). Bilionário dono da Space X, da Tesla e do X liderará estudo militar sobre guerra, segundo o Pentágono.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o fundador e CEO da SpaceX e da xAI, Elon Musk, falam com jornalistas na entrada da Casa Branca após um almoço com líderes do setor de tecnologia na Sala Leste, em Washington. — Foto: Jonathan Ernst / Reuters

O bilionário Elon Musk voltará a assessorar oficialmente o governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , como um dos responsáveis por um estudo sobre o futuro da guerra, anunciou o Pentágono.

Em um discurso na quarta-feira (30) na base militar de Quantico, o chefe do Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, afirmou que o chamado "Projeto Meridian" será "uma iniciativa liderada pelas melhores mentes dos Estados Unidos para estudar o futuro da guerra".

"Estamos aproveitando uma fonte única de vantagem americana, uma que nossos adversários não têm: nossos inovadores, nossas grandes lideranças e nossos tecnólogos", disse Hegseth.

O anúncio de Hegseth consolidou a reaproximação de Musk e o governo Trump pouco mais de um ano após sua saída conturbada do Departamento de Eficiência Governamental (DOGE) e uma briga pública com Donald Trump , em maio de 2025.

Musk vai copresidir o Projeto Meridian ao lado de Palmer Luckey, cofundador da empresa de tecnologia de defesa Anduril Industries, e de Newt Gingrich, ex-presidente republicano da Câmara dos Representantes, de 83 anos.

Hegseth afirmou que o objetivo do projeto é "examinar criativamente o futuro e identificar os campos que devemos dominar e as capacidades que devemos aperfeiçoar".

Os integrantes do Projeto Meridian incluirão líderes do setor privado selecionados pessoalmente e especialistas de diversas áreas da inovação, do meio acadêmico e das políticas públicas.

Elon Musk apoiou Trump e contribuiu para seu retorno à Casa Branca no início de 2025, mas os dois protagonizaram uma ruptura muito midiática devido à política de gastos promovida pelo presidente.

Mais tarde, ele retomou suas contribuições a causas republicanas, incluindo doações bilionárias a candidatos e a grupos políticos conservadores.

Hegseth determinou que as conclusões do Projeto Meridian sejam finalizadas e apresentadas em um prazo de 120 dias.

articles.title: Copiloto que tentou derrubar avião passou por 'radicalização' | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista à rede de TV norte-americana Fox News, primeiro-ministro israelense também disse que saberá, 'em questão de dias', se Irã tem envolvimento com o caso. Copiloto esfaqueou piloto e tentou derrubar avião da FlyDubai que seguia para Tel Aviv na quarta-feira (31).
articles.summary: O primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, disse nesta quinta-feira (1º) que o copiloto havia passado por um processo de radicalização islâmica.
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro de Israel , Benjamin Netanyahu, disse nesta quinta-feira (1º) que o copiloto que esfaqueou o piloto de um voo da FlyDubai e tentou derrubar o avião na quarta-feira (31) havia passado por um processo de radicalização islâmica.

"Sabemos que ele passou por uma doutrinação radical islâmica", disse Netanyahu em entrevista à rede de TV norte-americana Fox News.

O premiê não deu detalhes sobre o suposto treinamento. Na quarta-feira, autoridades israelenses disseram que o copiloto, um cidadão de Omã, agiu sozinho e sem nenhuma ligação com qualquer grupo terrorista ou Estado.

Na entrevista, Netanyahu afirmou também que poderá determinar, "em questão de dias", se o Irã teve algum envolvimento com o incidente, que ele chamou de ataque terrorista.

Embora o primeiro-ministro e seu governo tenham insistido na versão de atentado, ele reconheceu, mais cedo, que ainda é cedo para determinar quem está por trás do incidente.

Netanyahu também adotou cautela ao ser questionado sobre uma possível participação iraniana.

“Vamos chegar à origem desse agressor, independentemente de ele ter cúmplices ou não”. No entanto, ele advertiu que “era cedo demais para dizer algo” quando questionado se havia alguma indicação de envolvimento iraniano, segundo declaração à Fox News.

À agência de notícias Reutes, o enviado de Israel para os Emirados Árabes Unidos afirmou que Netanyahu falou nesta quinta-feira com o presidente dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, sobre o caso. O enviado também afirmou que ainda não foi possível determinar os motivos do ataque.

O avião que transportava passageiros que estavam no voo da Flydubai com destino a Israel, saído dos Emirados Árabes Unidos e desviado para a Arábia Saudita após emitir um sinal de emergência, chega ao Aeroporto Internacional Ben Gurion, em Lod, perto de Tel Aviv, Israel. — Foto: Ammar Awad / Reuters

O embaixador israelense na ONU, Danny Danon, por sua vez, classificou o episódio como um "ataque terrorista". Ele afirmou à Fox News que Israel tinha "certeza" de que se tratava de um ataque cometido por um indivíduo radical, mas que ainda não havia uma ligação estabelecida com um Estado ou organização terrorista.

Após o incidente, a Flydubai suspendeu todos os voos para Israel.

O copiloto foi preso e interrogado após o pouso, que contou com a ajuda de tripulantes, segundo a FlyDubai. O homem tem nacionalidade de Omã e, em depoimento após ser preso, afirmou que agiu que agiu sozinho .

Homem que ajudou a impedir tragédia em avião para Israel foi recebido como herói por Netanyahu — Foto: Reuters

O israelense Yaniv Hayun era apenas um dos 180 passageiros do voo FZ1073 da FlyDubai desta quarta-feira (30), que saiu de Dubai , nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, com destino a Tel Aviv . Horas depois, no entanto, ele chegou a Israel como o herói do voo.

Hayun afirmou ter conseguido reverter a queda do avião, que perdeu o controle após o copiloto esfaquear o piloto, em um episódio classificado como atentado terrorista pelo governo de Israel.

Ao desembarcar no aeroporto de Ben Gurion, Yaniv Hayun, foi recebido como herói pelo primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu. Ao premiê, ele disse ter entrado na cabine ao perceber o confronto entre os dois pilotos.

"Eu puxei os controles para cima e parei a descida do avião", afirmou Hayun.

O israelense afirmou que séries especializadas em aviação ajudaram na ação. "Por sorte, eu assisti a Air Crash Investigation", afirmou.

"É simplesmente inacreditável o que você fez, sabe? Simplesmente inacreditável. Você não apenas salvou todos a bordo do avião. Você não sabe o que poderia ter acontecido com ele. Nós não sabemos o que teria acontecido", disse-lhe Netanyahu.

O voo FZ1073 da FlyDubai havia saído de Dubai, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, no início da manhã, com destino a Tel Aviv, em Israel. Quando já estava próximo do espaço aéreo israelense, o copiloto atacou o piloto, que reagiu, segundo o governo israelense.

O confronto entre os dois deixou a aeronave temporariamente sem controle e fez o avião despencar cerca de 4.300 metros em aproximadamente 30 segundos, segundo o site de monitoramento aéreo Flightradar24.

Passageiros perceberam o confronto e, com a ajuda de tripulantes, conseguiram conter o copiloto, segundo relatos de pessoas que estavam no voo.

Em um vídeo enviado a parentes, o israelense Itzhak Liber, que estava entre os passageiros, afirmou que "um homem descontrolado com uma faca esfaqueou um dos pilotos".

"Estamos aqui no avião vindo de Dubai. Estamos aqui no avião; havia um homem descontrolado com uma faca que esfaqueou um dos pilotos. Nós agimos e ajudamos o piloto", disse Liber. Outra passageira relatou " sangue por todo o lado ".

Sinais de emergência e pouso na Arábia Saudita

Passageiros ensanguentados após briga entre pilotos em voo da Flydubai rumo a Israel que foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita em 30 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/redes sociais

Os radares registraram o descontrole do voo. Quando o avião sobrevoava a Jordânia, vizinha de Israel, sinais de emergência começaram a ser emitidos pela aeronave. Um deles transmitiu o código de sequestro da aviação mundial , e a rota foi bruscamente alterada para a Arábia Saudita.

Apesar de ambos os pilotos estarem feridos, o avião pousou em segurança na cidade de Tabuk, na Arábia Saudita. A FlyDubai afirmou, em comunicado, que "a tripulação" fez a aterrissagem, mas não esclareceu quais membros da equipe fizeram o pouso . Passageiros, no entanto, relataram que pilotos que eram passageiros no voo comandaram o pouso.

Israel chegou a solicitar que caças sauditas escoltassem o voo durante a operação para o pouso, mas o pedido foi negado, segundo o próprio governo da Arábia Saudita.

O ministro da Segurança Nacional israelense, Itamar Ben Gvir, afirmou que o terrorista tinha como objetivo assassinar os israelenses a bordo — 100 dos 180 passageiros eram cidadãos de Israel, segundo o governo israelense.

O aeroporto saudita de Tabuk, onde o voo aterrissou, afirmou que tanto o piloto quanto o copiloto ficaram feridos e foram hospitalizados , e que passageiros também receberam atendimento. Horas depois, eles foram levados por outro avião e chegaram ao aeroporto de Ben Gurion, em Tel Aviv.

Segundo Netanyahu, a Arábia Saudita deteve e interrogou o copiloto e abriu uma investigação sobre o caso. A mídia israelense afirmou que o Mossad, a principal agência de inteligência do país e responsável por operações especiais e secretas, também está investigando o caso.

Horas depois, um segundo voo da Flydubai rumo a Tel Aviv fez um breve desvio em sua rota, segundo o FlightRadar24, porém retomou o caminho depois. O motivo do desvio não havia sido divulgado até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A Flydubai opera voos diários entre Dubai e Tel Aviv, uma rota muito utilizada por cidadãos israelenses.

A mãe de uma passageira que estava a bordo do voo disse à agência Reuters que a filha lhe contou ter ouvido gritos e que um homem pegou uma faca, colocou o piloto no chão e que havia sangue por toda parte.

"Ela me ligou [após aterrissar] e disse que eles ouviram vozes, alguém pediu ajuda. Era o piloto. Ele estava gritando: ‘Ajuda, ajuda, ajuda!’. O avião começou a perder o controle, então todas as pessoas começaram a gritar e acharam que iriam morrer", disse Yasmin Abu Kasis, com base no relato da filha Miriam.

"Depois de alguns minutos, outros dois pilotos assumiram o controle. Alguns israelenses correram até um homem, e nesse momento ele pegou uma faca e tentou matar o piloto. Eles seguraram a mão dele e o colocaram no chão. Havia muito sangue por toda parte" , completou Yasmin.

Ainda segundo Yasmin, os passageiros ficaram "estressados e em choque" com toda a situação.

articles.title: Brasileiras traficadas para a África retornam ao Brasil após resgate | G1
articles.standfirst: Irmãs viajaram para o exterior acreditando que trabalhariam em um salão de beleza na Tailândia, mas foram vítimas de uma rede de tráfico humano que as obrigavam a aplicar golpes contra vítimas no Brasil.
articles.summary: Irmãs viajaram para o exterior acreditando que trabalhariam em um salão de beleza na Tailândia, mas foram vítimas de uma rede de tráfico humano que as obrigavam a aplicar golpes.
articles.body:
As duas brasileiras de Uberaba , no Triângulo Mineiro, que foram traficadas para países da África após promessa de emprego retornaram ao Brasil. A informação foi confirmada nesta quinta-feira (1) à TV Integração pela ONG The Exodus Road Brazil e Clínica de Combate ao Trabalho Escravo (CCTE) da Unipac Uberaba, que acompanham o caso.

As mineiras, que são irmãs, faziam parte dos 23 brasileiros que foram retidos em agosto em Madagascar após afirmarem ter escapado de uma rede de exploração ligada a crimes cibernéticos. Elas viajaram para o exterior acreditando que trabalhariam em um salão de beleza na Tailândia.

Segundo a CCTE, as irmãs voltaram para o Brasil há duas semanas e usaram recursos próprios para retornar ao país, com a ajuda de uma arrecadação online. Os detalhes do retorno das mulheres não foram divulgados.

Irmãs foram vítimas de uma rede de tráfico de pessoas

A Exodus Road Brazil afirma que os brasileiros foram vítimas de uma rede de tráfico de pessoas e exploração para aplicação de golpes virtuais.

A organização, entretanto, ressalta que não é possível afirmar que todos os 23 integrantes do grupo sejam vítimas de tráfico, cabendo às autoridades brasileiras investigar individualmente a situação de cada pessoa.

A organização afirma que os brasileiros eram obrigados a aplicar golpes contra vítimas no Brasil, como falsas abordagens em nome da Polícia Federal e o chamado "golpe do amor", no qual criminosos estabelecem relacionamentos fictícios com as vítimas para obter dinheiro.

Primeiro, o grupo foi levado do Camboja , no Sudeste Asiático, onde teria permanecido por cerca de cinco meses em situação de exploração. Depois, para a capital de Madagascar, Antananarivo, em 19 de agosto, após uma operação policial contra uma rede de golpes virtuais.

Entre os integrantes do grupo estão as duas mulheres de Uberaba que viajaram acreditando que trabalhariam em um salão de beleza.

“Uma das minhas irmãs é cabeleireira e recebeu uma proposta para trabalhar em um salão de beleza na Tailândia. A outra recebeu uma proposta para trabalhar como recepcionista. Elas saíram do Brasil com essa promessa de trabalho no exterior”, relatou o irmão das duas uberabenses traficadas na ocasião.

Brasileiros pediram ajuda ao governo brasileiro para retornaram

No início de setembro, parte dos 23 brasileiros afirmaram não ter recursos para pagar as passagens de volta ao Brasil , após fugirem da rede de exploração. A informação foi confirmada pela Exodus Road Brazil na ocasião.

Segundo a organização, eles conseguiram confirmar que familiares de 11 pessoas fizeram a declaração de hipossuficiência à Defensoria Pública da União (DPU) na esperança de conseguir ajuda do Itamaraty.

Procurado pelo g1 na ocasião, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) informou que, apesar de a comprovação de hipossuficiência financeira ser um requisito necessário, ela, sozinha, não é suficiente para que o governo custeie o retorno dos brasileiros.

O Itamaraty também reforçou que a repatriação de brasileiros é uma medida excepcional e não constitui um direito automático.

🔍 Hipossuficiência é a condição em que uma pessoa não possui recursos financeiros suficientes para pagar taxas de um processo judicial ou contratar um advogado sem prejudicar o próprio sustento ou o de sua família.

O Itamaraty também afirmou, na data, que uma missão da Embaixada em Maputo em Moçambique, onde fica o consulado mais próximo, seria enviada a Madagascar para prestar assistência consular presencial ao grupo.

Durante as tratativas, o irmão das moradoras de Uberaba também afirmou à reportagem que a família não tinha condições de pagar as passagens de retorno, que custam aproximadamente R$ 5,5 mil até São Paulo, além do deslocamento posterior até Minas Gerais.

A ONG afirmou que os familiares das duas mulheres procuraram a Defensoria Pública da União (DPU) e comprovaram a situação de hipossuficiência.

Segundo a organização, por haver indícios de que os brasileiros tenham sido vítimas de tráfico internacional de pessoas, o Estado brasileiro deveria garantir proteção e condições para o retorno seguro.

A entidade também afirmou que o Brasil é signatário do Protocolo de Palermo, promulgado pelo Decreto nº 5.017/2004, e que o governo possui procedimentos específicos para o atendimento e a eventual repatriação de brasileiros vítimas de tráfico internacional.

🔍 O Protocolo de Palermo prevê medidas de proteção e assistência às vítimas de tráfico de pessoas e estabelece que o país de nacionalidade deve facilitar e aceitar o retorno da vítima, levando em consideração sua segurança.

Brasileiros são vítimas de tráfico humano após falsas vagas de emprego — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Segundo o Itamaraty, a legislação brasileira estabelece uma série de critérios e requisitos para que o governo possa custear o retorno de um brasileiro que esteja no exterior.

Entre eles está a apresentação da declaração de hipossuficiência emitida pela Defensoria Pública da União. Também é avaliado se o cidadão já foi repatriado anteriormente.

O ministério, no entanto, afirmou que esses elementos são "necessários, porém não suficientes" para a realização da repatriação.

Também são analisadas alternativas para viabilizar o retorno, como auxílio de familiares, amigos, empregadores ou redes de apoio no Brasil e no exterior.

Segundo o Itamaraty, também podem ser considerados programas oficiais de repatriação disponíveis no país onde o brasileiro está.

O órgão ainda detalhou que há mais de 5 milhões de brasileiros residentes fora do país. Entre as demandas de natureza consular estão o auxílio a cidadãos em situação de desvalimento, a assistência a brasileiros detidos e o atendimento em situações de catástrofes naturais, conflitos e crises políticas

Brasileiros ficaram em aeroporto até serem acolhidos por organização em Madagascar — Foto: Reprodução/The Exodus Road Brazil

Brasileiros estavam com os passaportes retidos

Após a operação policial contra a rede de exploração, os brasileiros foram liberados, mas permaneceram sem os passaportes, segundo relatos obtidos pela Exodus Road Brazil.

A ONG orientou que eles não deixassem o aeroporto diante do risco de serem perseguidos pela organização criminosa. Posteriormente, eles foram acolhidos por uma organização local e levados para uma casa, onde permanecem hospedados.

Missionários e outras entidades locais forneceram alimentação e itens básicos enquanto o caso era acompanhado e as alternativas para o retorno ao Brasil eram discutidas.

Segundo um dos familiares, os passaportes só seriam devolvidos mediante a compra das passagens para o Brasil.

O próprio Itamaraty afirma que alerta brasileiros desde 2022 sobre os riscos de aceitar ofertas de trabalho no exterior sem verificar a procedência das propostas.

Segundo o ministério, um alerta consular sobre o aliciamento de brasileiros foi publicado naquele ano e atualizado nos anos seguintes. A versão mais recente, de julho de 2026, trata especificamente dos riscos relacionados ao tráfico de pessoas para o Sudeste Asiático.

Segundo a Exodus Road Brazil, propostas com salários elevados, passagens aéreas, moradia e promessa de uma vida melhor são utilizadas por redes criminosas para atrair pessoas para outros países.

"É uma vulnerabilidade e um sonho. Sonho de ter uma vida melhor, sonho de comprar uma casa, sonho de viajar, sonho de ter um bom salário", afirmou Cintia Meirelles, representante da ONG.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra Christa Pike durante julgamento em 1996 | G1
articles.standfirst: Condenada por assassinato em 1995 sobreviveu a duas injeções letais e foi hospitalizada nesta quinta (1). Ainda não há informações sobre seu estado de saúde.
articles.summary: Condenada por assassinato em 1995 sobreviveu a duas injeções letais e foi hospitalizada nesta quinta (1). Ainda não há informações sobre seu estado de saúde.
articles.body:
Christa Pike, de 50 anos, condenada à morte por assassinato em 1995, sobreviveu a duas injeções letais durante sua execução no Tennessee, nos Estados Unidos, nesta quinta-feira (1º). Ela tinha 18 anos na época do crime e, caso a execução tivesse sido concluída, seria a primeira mulher executada no estado em mais de 200 anos. Um vídeo da época mostra a reação de Pike durante seu julgamento (veja acima).

Pike e o então namorado, Tadaryl Shipp, foram acusados da morte de Colleen Slemmer, de 19 anos, colega dos dois em uma instituição de treinamento profissional em Knoxville. A jovem foi espancada e esfaqueada. O caso teve ampla repercussão porque um pentagrama foi gravado no corpo da vítima, e outros elementos do crime alimentaram temores relacionados a cultos satânicos em meio ao chamado “pânico satânico” das décadas de 1980 e 1990.

Em 1996, Pike foi condenada à morte. Shipp, que tinha 17 anos na época do crime, recebeu pena de prisão perpétua com possibilidade de liberdade condicional.

Ainda não se sabe o estado de saúde de Christa após a tentativa frustrada de execução, mas ela está hospitalizada após sair da penitenciária em uma ambulância.

Christa Pike quando foi sentenciada, em 1996, e em mugshot de 2023 — Foto: Foto 1: WBIR-TV via AP / Foto 2: TDOC via AP

As autoridades do Tennessee informaram que não conseguiram executar Christa Gail Pike, mesmo após a administração de duas doses de um medicamento letal. Um especialista em pena de morte afirmou que se trata de uma falha sem precedentes.

Pike permaneceu viva e roncando alto após a tentativa de execução por injeção letal e foi retirada da prisão em uma ambulância, segundo seus advogados.

Após o incidente, a prisioneira foi levada ao hospital, porém não se havia notícias sobre seu estado de saúde. "Não fomos informados sobre seu estado de saúde”, disseram os advogados de Pike em comunicado.

Após a falha na execução de Pike, o governador do Tennessee, Bill Lee, ordenou uma investigação independente sobre o incidente e também suspendeu as execuções no estado até o fim do ano —havia apenas uma outra pena de morte planejada.

Segundo os advogados, as autoridades administraram duas doses de pentobarbital em Pike. Robin M. Maher, diretora-executiva do Death Penalty Information Center, afirmou que o que ocorreu com Pike é “algo único e sem paralelo”.

Pentobarbital: como age a droga usada em execução frustrada de Christa Pike

Ela disse que outras sete pessoas sobreviveram a problemas médicos decorrentes da incapacidade das equipes de execução de acessar uma veia para administrar os medicamentos, mas que ninguém havia permanecido vivo após receber as drogas usadas nas execuções.

“Não sentimos satisfação em estar certos, mas as preocupações levantadas pela senhora Pike se mostraram verdadeiras: acesso venoso difícil, veias rompidas, pentobarbital degradado, ausência de atendimento médico de emergência quando as coisas inevitavelmente dão errado, tudo isso sob um protocolo que continua envolto em sigilo.”

articles.title: Bombeiro de folga ajuda vítimas após avião cair em área rural de MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Militar passava pelo local quando percebeu o acidente e, com apoio de um brigadista florestal, prestou os primeiros atendimentos até a chegada das equipes de emergência.
articles.summary: Militar passava pelo local quando percebeu o acidente e, com apoio de um brigadista florestal, prestou os primeiros atendimentos até a chegada das equipes de emergência.
articles.body:
Um bombeiro militar que estava de folga ajudou a socorrer duas pessoas que sobreviveram à queda de uma aeronave na MT-010 , na saída de São José do Rio Claro , em Mato Grosso. O militar passava pelo local no momento do acidente e iniciou os primeiros atendimentos às vítimas , com auxílio de um brigadista florestal.

As duas pessoas envolvidas na ocorrência estavam conscientes e receberam atendimento inicial no local. O bombeiro atuou na estabilização das vítimas até a chegada da equipe de serviço do Corpo de Bombeiros, que isolou a área.

Além da queda da aeronave, o acidente provocou o rompimento de uma rede de energia elétrica nas proximidades . Por causa do risco, foi necessário acionar a concessionária responsável pelo fornecimento para realizar o desligamento da rede.

O rompimento dos cabos ainda provocou um princípio de incêndio em uma área com palha de milho próxima ao local da queda. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o fogo acabou se apagando sozinho.

Além da queda da aeronave, o acidente provocou o rompimento de uma rede de energia elétrica nas proximidades — Foto: Reprodução

Os dois sobreviventes foram encaminhados para uma unidade de atendimento médico. A identidade deles e o atual estado de saúde não foram divulgados.

As causas do acidente estão sendo investigadas pelas autoridades competentes.

Segundo dados da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac), a aeronave envolvida no acidente é do modelo PS-FLO, com capacidade para transportar duas pessoas. No registro, a situação de aeronavegabilidade consta como normal.

O avião de pequeno porte era utilizado em operações privadas e passou para um novo proprietário em abril deste ano.

Algumas peças do avião ficaram espalhadas pelo local — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Temporal causa estragos em feiras livres do Paraná e quebra vidros de rodoviária | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo Simepar, velocidade do vento chegou a 37,4 km/h no momento do temporal, na madrugada desta quinta-feira (1º).
articles.summary: Segundo Simepar, velocidade do vento chegou a 37,4 km/h no momento do temporal, na madrugada desta quinta-feira (1º).
articles.body:
Por volta das 5h20 desta quinta-feira (1º), um temporal atingiu cidades da região Norte do Paraná. Em Londrina e Cambé , feirantes enfrentaram as rajadas de vento e tiveram prejuízos.

Uma câmera de segurança registrou o momento do vendaval com chuva em Cambé. As imagens mostram a estrutura das barracas se deslocando, sendo que um feirante corre para evitar que uma delas seja levada pelo temporal. Ao lado, outras bancas acabam ficando sem as lonas que as cobrem. Assista acima .

Em Londrina, diversas barracas também não resistiram às rajadas. Segundo o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar), a velocidade chegou a 37,4 km/h.

Temporal na madrugada de quinta-feira (1º) causou estragos em Londrina e Cambé. — Foto: Uilson Moreno/Silvio Costa/RPC

Luciano Pantaroto, feirante há 36 anos, contou à RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, que o tempo estava "abafado" antes do temporal.

"Foi a quantidade de eu tirar a lona aqui, segurar, cobrir as coisas. Se eu não tivesse tirado, teria quebrado tudo. Teria quebrado tudo mesmo. E quem não tirou, quebrou. Quebrou muita banca hoje", Pantaroto explicou.

O boletim da Defesa Civil da cidade registrou quatro quedas de árvore e dois destelhamentos.

Estragos causados pelo temporal em Londrina em bancas da feira livre. — Foto: Silvio Costa

Às 7h15, a Companhia Paranaense de Energia (Copel) informou que 6,5 mil imóveis em Londrina permaneciam sem energia elétrica após o evento climático; 4,3 mil, em Apucarana; 3,3 mil, em Rolândia; 2,6 mil, em Assaí; e 1,5 mil, em Faxinal.

Na região Oeste, há 20,6 mil casas sem energia; na Noroeste, 11,8 mil; Campos Gerais e Centro-Sul, 7 mil; litoral, 4,1 mil; Região Metropolitana de Curitiba (RMC), 3,2 mil; e Sudoeste, 254.

Vidros da rodoviária de Londrina quebraram durante o temporal. — Foto: RPC

Os vidros do Terminal Rodoviário de Londrina José Garcia Villar, entre as plataformas de embarque e desembarque de ônibus metropolitanos, quebraram com a força do temporal.

A base da estrutura de ferro se desprendeu do chão, tombou e houve a queda das vidraças. Por isso, os passageiros foram remanejados para outras plataformas.

articles.title: Monotrilho da Linha 17-Ouro registra nova falha no 2º dia de ampliação do horário de funcionamento em SP; situação já foi normalizada | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Metrô, o problema foi causado pelo esvaziamento de uma locomotiva, na estação Brooklin, sentido Morumbi, entre 7h23 e 7h29.
articles.summary: Segundo o Metrô, o problema foi causado pelo esvaziamento de uma locomotiva, na estação Brooklin, sentido Morumbi, entre 7h23 e 7h29.
articles.body:
Trem da Linha 17-Ouro, do Monotrilho do Metrô, em operação na Zona Sul de São Paulo. — Foto: Divulgação/Metrô

O monotrilho da Linha 17-Ouro apresentou nova falha na manhã desta quinta-feira (1°), segundo dia de ampliação do horário de funcionamento da linha na Zona Sul de São Paulo.

Segundo o Metrô, o problema foi causado pelo esvaziamento de uma locomotiva, na estação Brooklin, sentido Morumbi, entre 7h23 e 7h29.

A circulação dos trens já foi normalizada e o Metrô pediu desculpas aos passageiros pelos transtornos provocados.

Por causa da nova falha, o intervalo entre os trens passou de 15 minutos, segundo relatos da reportagem da TV Globo.

Passageiros da Linha 17-Ouro, do Monotrilho, relataram problemas na operação na noite desta quarta-feira (30), primeiro dia da ampliação do horário de funcionamento da linha. — Foto: Paula Paiva Paulo/g1

Passageiros relataram ter sido informados de que a ocorrência estaria relacionada a um possível excesso de peso no trem. Segundo os usuários, houve necessidade de esvaziamento de um dos vagões, além de uma porta da composição apresentar problemas.

De acordo com o Metrô, "um trem apresentou uma falha de tração na estação Chucri Zaidan, na Linha 17-Ouro, às 18h43", no sentido Washington Luís.

Ainda de acordo com a empresa, seis minutos depois, o trem foi restabelecido e conseguiu prosseguir viagem. A operação da linha foi normalizada.

O Metrô informou que pediu desculpas pelos transtornos causados aos passageiros e que não houve impacto na operação.

A ocorrência aconteceu no primeiro dia em que a Linha 17-Ouro passou a funcionar das 6h às 22h. Antes, a operação ocorria de segunda a sexta-feira, das 9h às 16h.

A mudança também incluiu os sábados e, segundo o Metrô, aumentou de três para seis o número de trens em operação. Com isso, o intervalo médio previsto entre as viagens caiu de 18 para 9 minutos.

Cinco trens circulam entre Morumbi e Aeroporto de Congonhas no formato de “carrossel”, seguindo por uma via e retornando pela outra. Um sexto trem faz o trajeto de ida e volta entre Brooklin Paulista e Washington Luís.

Segundo o Metrô, a circulação simultânea de mais composições coloca a linha em uma configuração operacional mais complexa. A empresa afirmou que vai acompanhar o desempenho dos sistemas, dos equipamentos de via e manobra e da infraestrutura durante esta nova etapa.

A Linha 17-Ouro continua em operação transitória e sem cobrança de tarifa.

🏪 Lojas e quiosques funcionam das 14h às 20h

🍔 Praça de alimentação funciona das 12h às 21h

🍽️ Restaurantes funcionam das 12h às 22h

🎬 Cinema mantém programação normal de exibição

🍔 Quiosques e praça de alimentação funcionam das 11h às 23h

🏪 O comércio do centro de Feira de Santana não funciona aos domingos, como ocorre normalmente.

articles.body:
Um homem com transtorno do espectro autista (TEA) morreu atingido por uma bala perdida dentro de casa no Bairro Alto do Rosário, em Barbalha , no Cariri cearense. Dois suspeitos do crime foram presos nesta quarta-feira (30).

A vítima, identificada como Carlos Augusto dos Santos , o "Nim" , estava dentro da residência, com a porta da sala aberta, quando foi atingido pelo disparo na noite da última terça-feira (29).

Carlos Augusto dos Santos, o "Nim", morreu após ser atingido por uma bala perdida dentro de casa em Barbalha. — Foto: Reprodução

A suspeita da polícia é que a bala tenha batido na porta da casa dele e ricocheteado, lesionando o homem no braço e no peito. Ele chegou a ser socorrido, mas não resistiu ao ferimento.

"Nim" realizava trabalhos voluntários na Capela Mãe Rainha e era descrito pelas pessoas como uma "pessoa que não fazia mal a ninguém e gostava de ajudar". O sepultamento dele ocorre nesta quinta-feira (1º).

Cleberson Firmino dos Santos e Carlos Antônio dos Santos Júnior foram presos por suspeita de envolvimento na morte de Carlos Augusto dos Santos, o Nim. — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo uma fonte da polícia, os suspeitos de efetuar os disparos são Cleberson Firmino dos Santos e Carlos Antônio dos Santos Júnior , conhecido como "Sombra" ou "Júnior", capturados nesta quarta-feira.

Investigações da polícia apontaram que Cleberson e Carlos Antônio foram ao endereço em uma motocicleta e realizaram disparos na casa vizinha a da vítima , que seria de familiares de um desafeto deles. No entanto, uma das balas atravessou a parede e atingiu "Nim", que não era alvo dos suspeitos .

Imagens de uma câmera de segurança registraram a fuga dos criminosos e ajudaram a identificar a dupla.

No momento da captura dos investigados, os agentes apreenderam vestimentas e a moto usada no dia do crime.

Polícia apreendeu com os suspeitos roupas e a motocicleta usada no dia do crime. — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 US states
articles.summary: Gov Gavin Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians".
articles.body:
California has officially banned child marriage, with Governor Gavin Newsom signing legislation to end the practice that is still legal in 32 US states.

The new law, which will come into effect on 1 January, states people must be 18 to get married in the Golden State.

Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians and minors". He signed the bill into law with Courtney Stodden, whose parents allowed her to marry a 50-year-old Hollywood actor when she was just 16.

Stodden, who has been advocating to end the practice, called the change a "victory" and said survivors of child marriage should "never have been expected to carry this burden".

Stodden said she would "keep fighting until children are protected from marriage in all 50 states".

She was married to actor Doug Hutchison - known for roles in The Green Mile, A Time to Kill and I Am Sam - in 2011, spurring headlines internationally over the controversy and appearances on several reality programmes in the US, including the VH1 series Couples Therapy.

Other survivors of child marriage also applauded the new law.

"California has sent a clear message to the world today," Brittany Bee, a former child bride, told the BBC. "A message of hope for all children that they may be free from systemic violence. That they may choose their own path."

Bee told the BBC she was wed at the age of 17 to escape an abusive home - only to then be allegedly abused by her adult husband.

"I was just going from one prison to another," she explained. "People have the audacity to tell me that I made a choice - kids, they can't consent."

Bee and other child marriage survivors have been working for years to have child marriages banned in California and across the United States.

About a decade ago, the practice was still allowed across all US state but more and more states have been altering laws. California is the 18th to ban it since 2018.

In the state, there had been no legal age to wed, allowing children to get married as long as their parents consent and a judge signs off on the nuptials.

There was also no mechanism for people under 18 to get divorced and many girls say they were trapped in abusive and predatory relationships.

Unchained At Last, an advocacy group fighting to end child marriage across the US, said about 9,000 girls were wed each year in California and that almost all child marriages involved girls to adult men.

Advocates say that many in the US don't even know that child marriage is legal in so many US states, nor that is has led to allegations of abuse.

Sara Tasneem, who says she was forced to marry a man nearly twice her age when she was 15 years old, told the BBC that it felt "surreal" to finally have the state recognise that child marriage should be banned. She says she started lobbying for this herself in 2017.

She was introduced to her husband the morning of their arranged marriage.

"I was forced to be his wife and that day, my entire life changed," she told the BBC. She became a mother the following year, at the age of 16, and dropped out of school.

"To have seen the arc of this bill come to fruition has been a marathon," Tasneem said. "I'm just grateful that kids cannot get married after January 1, 2027 in California."

articles.title: Jeff Bezos pledged $10 billion to fight climate change in 2020; 6 years later, his Earth Fund is putting more than $25 million into Pacific ocean conservation
articles.summary: The Pacific is becoming a major focus of Jeff Bezos’ environmental philanthropy, with the Bezos Earth Fund announcing more than $25 million in new grants
articles.body: The Pacific is becoming a major focus of Jeff Bezos’ environmental philanthropy, with the Bezos Earth Fund announcing more than $25 million in new grants for ocean conservation across five Pacific nations. The latest funding is intended to help governments protect large areas of marine territory while developing longer-term plans for managing their waters. According to Bezos Earth Fund, it also brings the fund’s total awards under a wider $100 million Pacific commitment to $63.3 million.Bloomberg reported Bezos pledged $10 billion through the fund in 2020, with the money intended to be distributed by the end of 2030.Reportedly, almost seven years into that period, around $2.4 billion has been granted so far, leaving billions still to be allocated in the years ahead.Jeff Bezos expands Pacific ocean protection with $25 million in new grantsThe latest grants cover work in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu. Together, the projects are designed to support protection and sustainable management across more than 625,000 square miles of ocean. The money forms the second round of the Earth Fund’s $100 million Pacific pledge, known as Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity. The initiative has a target of helping protect at least 30% of the region’s waters by 2030. The first $37.5 million round was announced in 2025, bringing the combined value of the two rounds to $63.3 million.Papua New Guinea is expected to use funding towards creating its first large offshore marine protected area, while Tonga is expanding protected areas. Support will also go towards the Cook Islands’ Marae Moana ocean park and habitat protection planning in Kiribati and Vanuatu.Marine protected areas can impose different levels of restriction. In the most tightly protected zones, activities such as fishing, mining and other forms of extraction can be prohibited altogether.Lauren Sánchez Bezos leads Jeff Bezos’ latest Pacific conservation grantsLauren Sánchez Bezos is leading the latest Pacific grant round. She has been vice chair of the Bezos Earth Fund since its early period and has become a more prominent figure in the couple’s philanthropic work since marrying Bezos in June 2025. She also announced the first round of Pacific grants last year. Around the same period, the fund awarded $30 million through its AI Grand Challenge, supporting environmental applications including technology intended to identify plant species and help decode the songs of endangered birds.The Pacific programme also extends beyond individual national waters. A grant to conservation organisation Rare is intended to help governments develop some of the first proposals for protecting biodiversity in international waters under the UN High Seas Treaty, which took effect in January.Jeff Bezos backs Pacific ocean protection amid growing climate pressureThe new funding arrives as the South-West Pacific deals with increasing pressure from ocean warming and acidification. A July report from the World Meteorological Organization said those changes were affecting marine ecosystems and local economies.According to World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, executive secretary of the UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific said, “Across Asia and the Pacific, heat is intensifying multi-hazard risks, intersecting with food systems, public health, infrastructure and oceans, and placing new pressures on health and livelihoods. Early warning and early action save lives when alerts are timely, messages are trusted and last-mile delivery reaches the vulnerable.”The region experienced its second-warmest year on record in 2025, according to WMO, with marine heatwaves disrupting ecosystems and fisheries. The wider impacts extend into food systems, infrastructure, public health and livelihoods.The Earth Fund says its previous grants are already producing changes in the region. Following the latest awards, it said 17 of the Pacific’s 22 countries are now working on protecting or sustainably managing their waters. French Polynesia, one of the earlier recipients, established what the fund described as the world’s largest network of fully protected marine areas earlier this year. The network covers almost 625,000 square miles, while Niue has protected 40% of its national waters.Jeff Bezos’ $10 billion climate pledge still has $7.6 billion to deployThe Pacific programme is only one part of an unusually busy period for the Bezos Earth Fund. Since April, the organisation has announced $34 million for more sustainable fabrics, $26 million for wildfire detection and prevention, and $100 million for projects aimed at turning vacant urban land into parks across eight US cities, as reported by Bezos Earth Fund and Fortune. Another $100 million has been committed through a partnership with Leonardo DiCaprio’s Re to support efforts involving some of the world’s most threatened species.Bezos Earth Fund reported that he originally committed $10 billion to climate and environmental causes through 2030. The fund has awarded about $2.4 billion so far, leaving approximately $7.6 billion still to be distributed. Reaching the original target by the end of 2030. The fund has said it remains committed to meeting that deadline. Bloomberg reported in May that grantmaking had risen to at least $400 million during 2026 after falling to $183 million in 2025. Kelly Levin, the organisation’s chief of science, data and systems change, said the fund takes time to understand an area before deciding how to direct its money.Jeff Bezos compares the challenge of philanthropy with building AmazonThe amounts being discussed through the Earth Fund remain relatively small compared with Bezos’ personal fortune. Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index as per October 1 2026, valued him at about $273 billion, placing him third on its ranking at the time of the report. Bezos has previously spoken about the difficulty of philanthropy in an interview with CNN in 2022. He said, “The hard part is figuring out how to do it in a levered way.”“It’s not easy. Building Amazon was not easy. It took a lot of hard work, a bunch of very smart teammates, hard-working teammates, and I’m finding — and I think Lauren is finding the same thing — that charity, philanthropy, is very similar.”You use AI every day. articles.title: "I’m calling the cops": Kai Cenat threatens to sue Reggie after serious allegations involving RaKai
articles.summary: Kai Cenat has responded publicly after streamer Reginald “Reggie,” also known as “Lil Rodney Son,” made serious allegations involving him and fellow
articles.body: Kai Cenat has responded publicly after streamer Reginald “Reggie,” also known as “Lil Rodney Son,” made serious allegations involving him and fellow streamer RaKai. During a livestream, Reggie raised claims about RaKai and accused Kai of knowing about an alleged incident. RaKai has denied the allegations, while Kai has now threatened legal action against Reggie. The situation has quickly drawn attention across the streaming community, but the claims remain unverified, and there is no indication from the sources reviewed that a court has yet ruled on the matter.Kai Cenat responds to Reggie’s allegationsThe dispute escalated after Reggie discussed the allegations during an Instagram livestream on September 30. His comments came amid a broader fallout involving the Clover Boys and his relationship with members of the streaming group.Kai Cenat responded directly to Reggie and challenged him to take the matter to law enforcement if he had evidence supporting his claims. He also said he had decided to pursue legal action.“This is so serious. This is what I want you to do, Reggie. Tomorrow, when you wake up, call the cops. Call the cops and show them the evidence. Because guess what? I’m calling the cops. Yeah. Yeah, I’m suing you, brother. I’m suing you, bro.”Kai said the controversy had gone beyond an argument between online personalities. He claimed the accusations were affecting his family and his future.“And I still have sympathy for you because I know you’re not yourself, bro. But it’s gone too far. You’re playing with my name. You’re playing with my family’s food. You’re playing with my future kids’ food. That’s how deep it goes.”Kai also explained that he had not originally intended to sue Reggie. According to Kai, his position changed as the allegations continued.“I would never do that to you. I would never. I would never do that to you, bro. I would never do that to you, bro. And when you said I was gonna sue you, I wasn’t even gonna sue you.”His comments represent a significant escalation in a dispute that had largely unfolded through livestreams and social media posts.RaKai denies Reggie’s claims as controversy growsRaKai has separately rejected Reggie’s allegations about his childhood. In a statement shared on X on September 29, RaKai said he had never been abused or inappropriately touched while growing up. He later repeated that denial during an Instagram Live session and urged people not to accept everything circulating online as fact.The allegations emerged after Reggie spoke publicly about his own claimed childhood abuse during an earlier livestream. He then brought RaKai and Kai Cenat into the wider discussion, leading to a rapid spread of clips across social media.The controversy has also drawn reactions from other creators. Some have declined to get involved, while others have urged caution as competing claims continue to circulate online. Agent 00, for example, previously described the situation as messy and said he did not want to add to the discussion.Kai later posted the brief message “Put you first” on X without explaining what prompted it. The post appeared shortly after his comments about the dispute and his stated intention to take legal action.For now, the central claims remain allegations rather than established facts. RaKai has denied the allegations involving him, and Kai has disputed Reggie’s statements by threatening a lawsuit. Whether legal proceedings actually follow will determine the next stage of the dispute.The episode also highlights how quickly personal conflicts among major streamers can move from private disagreements to public controversies. With millions of followers watching, livestream comments and social media clips can spread before the underlying claims have been independently established.You use AI every day. articles.title: Captain Machchhar, a dentist, plumber & the crew who helped save over 170 lives on flydubai flight
articles.summary: When Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv, he was left bleeding on the floor as the plane plunged
articles.body: When Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv, he was left bleeding on the floor as the plane plunged thousands of feet.But even while seriously injured, the Mumbai-born pilot managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to rush in, overpower the attacker and regain control of the aircraft.What followed was a desperate chain of interventions by people on board, including passengers, a dentist and off-duty pilots, that helped save over 170 people aboard Flight 1073.Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Machchhar a “hero”, while Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised his actions in helping passengers and crew overpower the attacker.Captain Smit MachchharMachchhar, an Indian citizen from Mumbai, was stabbed by his fellow pilot, an Omani national, during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The attack sent the Boeing 737 MAX into a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds.Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to release the cockpit door, allowing people outside to enter.Netanyahu said Machchhar “fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door” and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker.Machchhar was taken to hospital after the plane landed safely in Tabuk, north-western Saudi Arabia. Indian officials said he was in stable condition and were in contact with his family.He had trained at New Zealand’s Mainland Air for 18 months in 2008 and 2009. The airline’s chief executive Philip Kean described him as an above-average pilot and said training for emergencies was one thing, but successfully handling such a situation in reality was “a whole different story”.Yaniv HayounAmong the passengers who entered the cockpit was Yaniv Hayoun, whom Netanyahu described as a plumber.Hayoun said Machchhar was lying injured on the other side of the cockpit door when passengers entered and confronted the attacker.As people wrestled with the pilot, Hayoun said he moved towards the controls and began pulling them back, using what he had seen on television as his reference.Other crew members then took over and helped stabilise the aircraft.Dr Shota MusaevDr Shota Musaev, a dentist travelling on the flight, was another passenger who rushed towards the cockpit.He told CNN that he found the attacker on top of Machchhar, stabbing him.Musaev said the captain was covered in cuts, particularly on his head and hands, and had lost a large amount of blood.He feared Machchhar would die before help arrived.Musaev also helped restrain the attacker, using headphone cords and plastic zip ties to tie him up.The off-duty pilotsPassengers also reported that two relief pilots were travelling on the aircraft and entered the cockpit during the emergency.One passenger, Almog Itali, said the relief pilots included a British pilot and helped pull the aircraft up, stabilise it and guide it towards Saudi Arabia.Other reports differed on their nationalities, with some identifying them as South African or New Zealand pilots.Their exact role has not been independently established in the accounts available, but passengers said they were among those who helped regain control of the aircraft.The rescue was not the work of one person.Passengers and crew members entered the cockpit after Machchhar opened the door and helped overpower the attacker.Their intervention came as the plane was struggling to recover from its steep descent.One passenger described the plunge as feeling like “massive turbulence” lasting 20 to 30 seconds.The aircraft eventually landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.Aviation experts said the forces involved were severe. Former United Airlines pilot and aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said he was surprised the aircraft did not break apart, while another expert said the remaining altitude may have been crucial to the recovery.Flight 1073 ended in a safe landing and the people on board made it possible.You use AI every day. articles.title: Christina Pike, first Tennessee woman set for execution in 200 years, survives 2 lethal injections
articles.summary: Tennessee officials were unable to execute Christa Gail Pike on Wednesday after administering two doses of the lethal injection drug, in what a death
articles.body: Tennessee officials were unable to execute Christa Gail Pike on Wednesday after administering two doses of the lethal injection drug, in what a death penalty expert described as an unprecedented failure. Pike remained alive after the attempted execution and was taken by ambulance to a hospital, her attorneys said.Pike, 50, had been scheduled to be executed at 10 am (local time) for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom she killed when she was 18. She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.Pike’s attorneys said she was alive and loudly snoring after the second dose of pentobarbital. They filed an emergency motion with the Tennessee Supreme Court seeking to halt the execution, arguing that she was in “unnecessary agony” and that the attempt violated her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment.Tennessee Gov Bill Lee ordered “a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred” and said the remaining execution scheduled for this year would not take place.“Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State’s most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective,” Lee said.The Tennessee Department of Correction said officials “followed every step of the State’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office.”The state’s protocol provides for a second set of drug syringes to be administered “if the inmate is not deceased” after the first set, but does not specify what should happen if the person remains alive after the second dose.Robin M. Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said what Pike experienced is “singular and unparalleled.” She said seven other people have survived medical problems during executions because teams were unable to access a vein for lethal injection, but no one had remained alive after receiving the drugs used in such executions.Media witnesses said the execution chamber curtains were raised at 7.27 pm (local time), showing Pike strapped to a gurney. During her final statement, she said, “I’m going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life and that is in love,” and described herself as at peace.Pike remained awake and at one point raised her head and asked prison officials if her arm was supposed to feel that way. It was not immediately clear what she was referring to. By 8.26 pm (local time), witnesses reported that the second dose of pentobarbital had been administered.Pike continued to be heard snoring behind the closed curtain until the microphone was cut off at 8.53 pm (locsl time), after which media witnesses were escorted from the area.The failed execution was the second time this year that Tennessee was unable to carry out a lethal injection. In May, state officials halted the execution of Tony Carruthers after executioners spent more than an hour trying and failing to place an IV to administer pentobarbital.The failed execution came after a legal battle over whether Pike’s allegations of childhood sexual abuse had been fully considered at sentencing. The 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals had issued a stay shortly before the scheduled execution, but the US Supreme Court later cleared the way for the execution to proceed. The court’s conservative majority did not explain its order, while its three liberal members dissented.Pike did not deny killing Slemmer, but her supporters argued that her age at the time of the crime, mental illness and allegations of severe sexual abuse should be considered. After the killing, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.“I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” Pike said in a statement.Pike and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, were convicted in the fatal stabbing and beating of Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville, on January 12, 1995. Prosecutors said Pike lured Slemmer to a wooded area because she feared Slemmer was trying to take her boyfriend.Pike cut Slemmer with a box cutter and beat her with a large piece of asphalt. Shipp, who was 17 at the time, admitted to carving a pentagram into Slemmer’s body. He received a life sentence with the possibility of parole, while Pike was sentenced to death.Slemmer’s mother, May Martinez, had travelled to Nashville hoping to witness the execution after waiting decades for Pike’s sentence to be carried out.“Every time I think about it, I think about Colleen feeling that pain and trying to get up and run,” Martinez told The Associated Press in a telephone interview on Saturday.Since the Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty in 1976, 18 women have been executed in the US, accounting for about 1% of all executions, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.Tennessee announced in 2024 that it was switching from a three-drug lethal injection protocol to the single drug pentobarbital. The change came more than two years after the state halted the execution of Oscar Smith and acknowledged that its lethal injection drugs had not been properly tested.You use AI every day. articles.title: A New Jersey woman paid $25 for a mouldy table at a garage sale; 30 years later, it was identified as a rare 18th-century card table made by John Seymour & Son and sold for $541,500
articles.summary: A New Jersey schoolteacher who bought a mouldy, pitch-black table at a garage sale for just $25 ended up owning a rare piece of American furniture worth
articles.body: A New Jersey schoolteacher who bought a mouldy, pitch-black table at a garage sale for just $25 ended up owning a rare piece of American furniture worth more than half a million dollars. Claire Wiegand-Beckmann purchased the table roughly three decades before it appeared on Antiques Roadshow, when she was moving into a new home and wanted a small table. She initially saw little reason to believe it was valuable. But when furniture expert Leigh Keno examined it in Secaucus, New Jersey, in 1997, he discovered an original maker's label identifying it as the work of Boston cabinetmakers John and Thomas Seymour. The table was later sold at Sotheby's for $490,000, with the buyer's premium bringing the total to $541,500.From a $25 garage-sale table to a rare 18th-century discoveryWiegand-Beckmann came across the table at a garage sale in New Jersey while she was moving into a new house. She told Antiques Roadshow that she needed a small table and thought the piece might work for the space.It was hardly an obvious treasure. She recalled that it was “pitch black” and “a moldy mess” when she saw it outside at the sale. The seller had priced it at $30, but Wiegand-Beckmann said she had only $25 with her. The seller agreed to accept the lower amount, allowing her to take the table home.The purchase was made roughly 30 years before her appearance on Antiques Roadshow. For years, the table was simply a piece of furniture in her Bergen County home. At the time she bought it, there was no indication that the seemingly battered table was a significant example of early American furniture.The turning point came in 1997, when Antiques Roadshow held an event in Secaucus, New Jersey. Wiegand-Beckmann decided to bring the table along to see whether experts could tell her more about it.The table reportedly arrived in an unusual fashion. Because it was awkward and wobbly, Wiegand-Beckmann brought it into the event upside down on a cart. That made the object look even less like an important piece of antique furniture.It was examined by furniture specialist Leigh Keno, who immediately began looking at its construction, decorative inlay and other characteristics. But one detail proved especially important: the table still had its original maker's label.The label read John Seymour and Son, Creek Square, Boston. Keno explained that surviving furniture with an original label from the makers was exceptionally rare.Experts identify a rare Federal-period tableKeno identified the piece as a Federal inlaid mahogany demi-lune card table made by John and Thomas Seymour, Boston cabinetmakers working in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.The table is dated to about 1794. PBS classifies it as an 18th-century piece and identifies its material as mahogany. Keno highlighted its figured mahogany, satinwood inlay and distinctive decorative details as evidence of its quality.The Seymour name was particularly significant. John and Thomas Seymour were prominent Boston furniture makers whose work was produced for wealthy families of the period. The surviving label gave specialists an unusually direct connection between the table and its makers.Keno told Wiegand-Beckmann that the table was an exceptional example of Federal furniture. Its craftsmanship, original features and maker's label all contributed to its importance.The $25 table was appraised at up to $300,000The discovery transformed Wiegand-Beckmann's expectations. When Keno examined the table in 1997, the initial auction estimate was $200,000 to $300,000. The appraiser suggested that on a particularly good day it could potentially bring $300,000.That was already an extraordinary increase from the $25 garage-sale price.PBS later updated the auction valuation for the piece to 400,000-600,000 in its records. The broadcaster also notes that valuations can change over time depending on market conditions and the circumstances of a sale.The original $25 purchase price therefore represented only a tiny fraction of what specialists believed the table could command at auction.The table heads to Sotheby'sAfter the Antiques Roadshow appraisal, Wiegand-Beckmann contacted Keno about selling the table. The process eventually took it to Sotheby's in New York, where it was offered as part of the auction house's Important Americana furniture and folk art sale in January 1998.The auction attracted collectors interested in American furniture. Bidding quickly moved far beyond the original estimate.According to PBS's later account of the auction, bidding reached $490,000, at which point the table was sold. The $490,000 figure was the hammer price. Once Sotheby's buyer's premium was added, the total selling price reached $541,500.The auction result was described by PBS as a world record for Federal furniture at the time.From a garage sale to a $541,500 auctionThe transformation was extraordinary. Wiegand-Beckmann had paid $25 for a table that looked dirty, damaged and unremarkable. Around three decades later, that same piece became a highly sought-after example of Federal-period American furniture.The difference between the purchase price and auction result was enormous. The $541,500 final price, including the buyer's premium, was 21,660 times the $25 that Wiegand-Beckmann had originally paid.The table's value was not simply a consequence of its age. Its rarity, original label, original finish, craftsmanship and association with John and Thomas Seymour all played important roles. Keno specifically noted that the label was unusually valuable evidence because labelled examples of the makers' work were rare.Why the original condition matteredOne of the unusual aspects of the story is that the table's battered appearance could easily have encouraged its owner to clean or refinish it extensively.Wiegand-Beckmann told the Antiques Roadshow team that she had used linseed oil and turpentine on the table but did not refinish it. That proved significant because retaining its original finish helped preserve the characteristics that specialists valued.Keno later explained that the table's rarity, original label and original finish were among the factors that made it such an important piece.A $25 purchase becomes an American furniture landmarkThe story has remained one of Antiques Roadshow's most memorable discoveries because the table looked so ordinary when Wiegand-Beckmann bought it. She had gone to a garage sale looking for a small piece of furniture, negotiated the price down to what she could afford and took home what appeared to be a battered old table.Instead, she had acquired a rare example of Federal-period craftsmanship by two important Boston cabinetmakers.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1899, nine-year-old Thomas Gilcrease received 160 acres; 18 years later, it had 32 producing oil wells, and his wealth later helped build Tulsa's Gilcrease Museum
articles.summary: Thomas Gilcrease was just nine-year-old when he became eligible for a 160-acre land allotment in Oklahoma through his Creek tribal membership in 1899.
articles.body: Thomas Gilcrease was just nine-year-old when he became eligible for a 160-acre land allotment in Oklahoma through his Creek tribal membership in 1899. The land, near present-day Glenpool, later became part of the Glenn Pool oilfield, where oil was discovered in 1905. By 1917, 32 producing wells were operating on his property, giving Gilcrease the income to continue his education and eventually build a career in the oil industry. That wealth later supported his growing interest in American Indian history, art and culture.Gilcrease was born in 1890, in Robeline, Louisiana, the eldest child of his parents, according to Oklahoma Historical Society. His family moved to the Creek Nation in Oklahoma Territory soon after his birth and eventually settled at Wealaka. His Creek ancestry came through his mother, while his father was non-Indian.His name was entered on the Creek tribal rolls when he was nine which made him eligible for the 160-acre allotment under the Dawes Commission process. At the time, the value of the land was not yet tied to the oil wealth that would later come from it. Six years after Gilcrease received the allotment, the Glenn Pool oilfield was discovered in 1905 and by 1917, the property had 32 producing oil wells.The income from the land helped Gilcrease continue his education. He had attended rural one-room schools before studying at Bacone College and the Kansas State Teacher's College in Emporia.At Bacone, one of his teachers was Alexander Posey, who taught Gilcrease about the Trail of Tears and American Indian leaders such as Sequoyah and Sitting Bull. He learnt about making bows and arrows, hunting and the operations of the Creek National Council at Okmulgee. These lessons became part of a wider interest in American Indian history that remained important to Gilcrease throughout his life.Gilcrease becomes art collectorOil became an important part of Gilcrease's working life. He eventually worked in several fields, including ranching, farming, banking and the oil industry. In 1922, he founded the Gilcrease Oil Company. His company later brought in numerous wells in Oklahoma, Texas and Kansas.Gilcrease also discovered a new oil-producing strata near Wetumka. It became known as the Gilcrease sand. His business interests expanded further, and he obtained controlling interests in several banks, including the Fourth National Bank of Tulsa, the Bank of Bixby and state banks in Coweta and Wagoner.While his oil business was growing, so was his interest in art. Gilcrease bought his first painting, Rural Courtship by Daniel Ridgway Knight, in 1912. He later travelled to Europe to study fine art and petroleum. According to the Gilcrease museum. During these trips, he became interested in building a collection connected to American Indian history and the American West.Gilcrease gathered American Indian art and artefacts, books, manuscripts, maps and other historical material. He also became involved in archaeological work and personally excavated Indian archaeological sites in the United States and Mesoamerica.Building the dream museumGilcrease's collecting became more active during the 1930s and 1940s. In 1942, he established the Thomas Gilcrease Foundation to gather, maintain and preserve material related to American Indians. A year later, he opened his first museum in San Antonio, Texas.Gilcrease had moved his company headquarters to San Antonio in 1937 to be closer to his major field operations. However, the museum did not attract enough public interest there. He closed the display in 1947 and moved his collection back to Tulsa.In May 1949, Gilcrease opened a new museum in Tulsa. The building stood beside his home west of downtown. The collection continued to grow as he acquired paintings, books, photographs, manuscripts and other historical material.One of the major additions came in 1944, when Gilcrease purchased Dr Philip G Cole's Western art collection. The purchase included 636 works of art, along with books, photographs and archival material. It also brought paintings by Frederic Remington and works by Charles M Russell into his collection.Another major acquisition came in 1948, when Gilcrease acquired the estate of landscape painter Thomas Moran. It contained about 2,000 works of art, including watercolours of the Yellowstone region of Montana and Wyoming. He also acquired an important collection of art and correspondence connected to George Catlin, as well as works by Alfred Jacob Miller.Gilcrease's collection also included works by artists such as Winslow Homer, John Singer Sargent and James McNeill Whistler. During visits to the artists' colony at Taos, New Mexico, he bought paintings directly from artists including Ernest Blumenschein and Bert Phillips. He also collected the work of Native American artists including Acee Blue Eagle, Woody Crumbo and Willard Stone.Tulsa secures ollectionThe scale of Gilcrease's collecting eventually created financial difficulties. By 1953, he was financially strained and owed about $2.5 million to business associates, galleries and art brokers for various acquisitions.The City of Tulsa then organised a bond issue in 1954 to pay Gilcrease's debts and secure his collection for the community. In 1955, Gilcrease transferred the title to his collection to the city. The museum was renamed the Thomas Gilcrease Institute of American History and Art.In 1958, Gilcrease also deeded the museum buildings and more than 13 acres of land to the community. Revenue from some of his oil properties was committed towards repaying the original bond amount. That repayment was completed in 1985.Gilcrease, however, continued collecting after the transfer of his collection to Tulsa. His interest in archaeology and ethnology also led him to support field excavations of Indian mounds in the Mississippi Valley. Material from those excavations and his later collecting eventually reached the museum through a bequest after his death in 1962.The collection continued to expand after Gilcrease's death. The museum now houses more than 12,000 works of fine art, while its Helmerich Center for American Research holds about 100,000 rare books, manuscripts and other archival materials.The museum's collections also include more than a quarter of a million artefacts related to the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. The collection had grown to include 10,000 works of American Indian and related art, 250,000 artefacts and 100,000 rare books when the collection was presented to the people of Tulsa in 1955.You use AI every day.
